
==My Story==

In 1995 or so, I randomly picked up a book my sister was reading. This was [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/The_Fires_of_Heaven The Fires of Heaven]. She said a friend of her's has been reading it, but I didn't know it at the time. The cover art was very interesting and I had been looking for something to read. I didn't really know what was going on. I did remember this weird feeling reading the book. I had never felt this before when I read another book. It was very alien, being dumped into the middle of Rhuidean in the middle of ruins, and random shadow hounds appearing out of nowhere. I didn't read into that far at that time.

The public school system I went to did not have busing. Most of the kids who could drive, did. Before I figured out that walking 40mins back home meant that I could set my own curfew, I hanged out at the public library, waiting for my dad to come pick me up. He was a post-doctorate, meaning that no one knew when he was going to show up. My dad certainly didn't. And since I didn't particularly cared to do homework, I ended up trolling the library bookshelves.

This library was cavernous. The main lobby had a vaulted ceilings at least two stories high. It was divided into two primary wings, an adult section and a kids section. Fantasy and sci-fi paperbacks were kept on these spinning, wireframe shelves. I would go and spin them like roulette and randomly pick out books that catch my fancy. As a sophomore in high school, I had already gotten bored of the kids section, and I had exhausted most of the fantasy and sci-fi books in the young adults section. I started trolling through the adults section.

I had seen [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/The_Eye_of_the_World The Eye of the World] often and avoided it. I knew it was related to [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/The_Fires_of_Heaven The Fires of Heaven]. There was a weight that came with [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/The_Fires_of_Heaven The Fires of Heaven], and so I kept avoiding it.

And one day, I got fed up with being unable to find a book I wanted to read. I pulled [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/The_Eye_of_the_World The Eye of the World] off the shelf and took it to a cubicle at the basement, where the librarians kept the reference books. Sticking my head into the cubicle-desk, cutting off my vision of the rest of the room, I started reading. I was so drawn into the world, I forgot about being hungry. My dad had came by the library late that day, and there I was, well past seven in the evening, totally absorbed into the adventures of Rand, Mat, Perrin, and Egwene.

Since then, I've grown up some (I hope) and read many more fiction books. I have pursued one of my life's passions -- martial arts, also catalyzed by that particular library. (I still have the book that really got me dreaming). I've really only found one other author whose work I read as a guide to life -- Robert A. Heinlein. Yet, Heinlien's book never elicited the passion I have for Jordan's [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/Wheel_of_Time Wheel of Time], certainly not enough to dig up a wikia and start contributing towards it.

My main reason for being here at this wikia relates to the martial arts. About four (five?) years ago, I attended the Altanta DragonCon. This was probably the second year they had a Wheel of Time track. I attended several sessions, one of them including a session demonstrating the [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/Sword_forms sword forms].

I walked away disgusted.

Looking back now, I didn't know as much then as I thought I did. (That bodes well for the future, don't you think?). The panel members had varying experiences in the martial arts and there were at least a few people that had experience with sword play. The panel organizer told us, the audience, they got their list of sword forms from what was effectively an internet meme. It wasn't complete. There were no citations, and it was obvious, some of the demonstrations came from descriptions that were made up. These organizers encouraged the audience to help them out and improve it.

I didn't know much, but I had enough experience with forms that many applications were fairly non-obvious. You could render them into simple punch-block-strikes, but there were a lot more to it than that. Oftentimes, the names were poetic that captured the essence of the idea in the form. Sometimes they were ironic and humerous. Sometimes (in the case of xingyiquan "Water Strider"), it looked like one of the teachers forgot the name and, when asked by a student, made it up on the spot.

What it comes down to is that, the interpretations from that list was to me, made by a gamer. I play video games and RPGs too. I've GMd a few games as well. I know how gamers think. You start thinking in terms of "Level 10 Cat Crosses the Courtyard" gives you +5 to defense, and +3 to Charisma when trying to use Bluff or Intimidate. That was what disgusted me.

About a year ago, I got it in my head to try this project again. I'd compile a list together and present it to my martial arts buddies to see if the names evoked any feelings from their own arts. I sat down and started listing sword forms as they appeared in the books. I got most them all the way up through [http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/Knife_of_Dreams Knife of Dreams]. I came ''here'' in a roundabout way -- I was looking for a map of Terry Goodkind's novels, and realized that wikia.com probably had a wiki devoted to WoT fandom. And so, hopped on caffeine, I started adding stuff.

My main motivation with the sword form page(s) is to compile together the ''canon'' for WoT sword forms. This includes books and interviews with Jordan. I know in the martial arts, even within the same training hall, people have vastly different opinions on form interpretations. You can at least test out whether someone is full of crap or whether they can say anything they want: you can feel their power and skill. It starts getting worse when you encounter people only superficially involved in the martial arts, but generally, are armchair experts. These people have the least respect among martial artists, simply because their opinion is not backed by skill. Then, there are gamers who view the combat art through the lenses of game mechanics. I can forgive them because, well, I like playing games too. They exercise the strategic and tactical mind. Finally, there are the vast, undifferentiated masses of people who don't consider themselves experts at martial arts, and since they have not been initiated into those mysteries, have a lot of well-meaning but incorrect concepts. I don't mind those people because most of the time, they don't present themselves as experts ... and even if they do, their opinions don't matter.

Coming to the WoT fandom, though, means there are a lot of opinions about these sword forms. Some are informed through physical experience, some are not. Some folks are fascinated by it and don't want to have their dreams invaded by reality. That's all OK. I think the best way to manage all of that is to stay as close to canon as possible.

I still want to see if I can reconstruct these sword forms into workable sword play. It'll probably take years. It won't be put on this site. I do want a credible source of canon when I do, so at least, if I start saying things in opposition, people at least can distinguish the fandom from experiment.

[http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/User:Qaexl Qaexl] 22:26, February 18, 2010 (UTC)
